sources_quoted.text: Enemy champions within {{tt|700 units|center to edge}} of you become cursed, causing them to receive {{as|12% increased magic damage|magic damage}} from all sources.
sources_quoted.reading: Enemy-side aura debuff. Amplifier magnitude = x1.12. Scope of the amplified damage = MAGIC damage only. Scope of the sources = any attacker (self or ally). Applies to cursed ENEMY champions, i.e. never to damage the mask holder receives.

sources_quoted.text: {{tip|Immobilize|Immobilizing}} an enemy champion marks them as ''Vulnerable'' for 4 seconds, increasing the damage they take from all sources by 7%. Subsequent immobilizes against a target extend the duration of the effect.
sources_quoted.reading: Per-target enemy-side amp, magnitude x1.07, applies to ALL damage types (contrast with Unmake, which is magic-only). Imperial Mandate carries no flat bonus-damage proc in this cache (60 AP / 15 AH / 150% mana regen and the 'Control' 20-AH passive are the rest of the item).

sources_quoted.text: Dealing {{as|magic damage}} to an enemy champion with a [[champion ability]] applies a stack of ''Vile Decay'' to them for 6 seconds, stacking up to 4 times and up to once per basic attack or ability per {{tip|cast instance}} every {{fd|0.3}} seconds. Each stack inflicts {{as|{{fd|7.5}}% magic resistance reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|mr}} at 4 stacks.
sources_quoted.reading: Considered as the alternative explanation for the delta (the scenario id contains 'curse'), because MR reduction also changes post-mitigation damage. Rejected below on numeric grounds.

sources_quoted.text: Independent damage value modifiers distinct from resistances: percentage damage amplification, percentage damage reduction, and flat damage reduction; percent modifiers stack multiplicatively with each other and with resistance-based reduction.
sources_quoted.reading: Vulnerable (7%) and Unmake (12%) compose multiplicatively: x1.07 * x1.12 = x1.1984.

step_1_delta_shape.note: The two baselines differ by a pure multiplicative factor of 1.11990, and by exactly 20.0 absolute.

step_2_match_against_sourced_magnitudes.result: MATCH (exact, and independent of the target's MR)

step_2_match_against_sourced_magnitudes.candidate: Bloodletter's Curse Vile Decay stack-count change (7.5% MR reduction per stack)
step_2_match_against_sourced_magnitudes.check: Required ratio window from 1-dp rounding is (186.75/166.85, 186.85/166.75) = (1.11927, 1.12054). Scanning integer target MR 20..259 and every stack pair a->b: the 0->4 stack case (the natural 'full stacks vs none' one) has NO integer-MR solution (MR 55 gives 1.11913, MR 56 gives 1.12069 - the window falls between them). Only contrived combinations survive: 0->3 at MR 90/91, 1->4 at MR 85, 0->2 at MR ~246-253, 1->3 at MR ~208-213, 2->4 at MR ~180-183 - all requiring the enemy to carry heavy MR items AND a stack-count change rather than an amp change.
step_2_match_against_sourced_magnitudes.result: NOT REJECTED OUTRIGHT, but strictly weaker than the exact, MR-independent 1.12 match

independent_computation.step_3_conclusion_on_what_moved: The delta is exactly ONE application of Abyssal Mask 'Unmake' (x1.12) on this event. Imperial Mandate's 7% Vulnerable factor did not move (a 7% change would have produced 178.5, not 166.8); if Vulnerable is present it is present in both baselines.

step_4_worked_instantiation.purpose: Show that both baselines are reachable from one coherent damage state, so the delta really is a single 1.12 factor rather than a different pre-amp damage.
step_4_worked_instantiation.example: raw 300 magic vs target MR 100 carrying one Vile Decay stack (100 * (1 - 0.075) = 92.5): post = 300 * 100/(100+92.5) = 155.844; * 1.07 (Vulnerable) = 166.753 -> 166.8; * 1.12 (Unmake) = 186.764 -> 186.8. Generic form: base_post_mitigation ~= 155.89, x1.07 = 166.8 (new), x1.07 x1.12 = 186.8 (old).
step_4_worked_instantiation.note: The instantiation is illustrative; the scenario's champion/target configuration lives in scripts/ and was deliberately NOT read.

independent_computation.step_5_rule_applied: Per the cached Unmake text, the x1.12 factor is legal on a damage event if and only if ALL of: (a) the damage type is magic, (b) the recipient is an enemy champion under the curse aura, and (c) it is applied exactly once. It is illegal on physical or true damage (Unmake is type-scoped to magic; only Imperial Mandate's Vulnerable is 'damage they take from all sources'), illegal on damage received by the mask holder or its allies, and illegal a second time on the same event.
independent_computation.step_6_verdict_derivation: The new baseline is the old baseline with exactly one Unmake application removed. Removing it is correct in every case except one: event 13 being a single, first-and-only application of Unmake to magic damage received by a cursed enemy (in which case 'from all sources' makes the amp mandatory even when the attacker is an ally, and 186.8 would be right). The scenario is a ROSTER fight - the configuration that first mixes damage types (ally/enemy autos and AD abilities alongside the AP holder's magic), mixes damage directions (the holder also receives damage), and multiplies the layers an amp can be applied at. Those are exactly the conditions under which an untyped, holder-scoped 'target takes +12%' implementation over-applies, and none of them is a condition under which a correctly-typed implementation under-applies. Two sourced asymmetries decide it: Unmake is the only amp in this scenario that is damage-type-scoped (Vulnerable is 'all sources', Unmake is 'magic damage'), and only Unmake's factor moved - i.e. the change is precisely a scoping change on the one effect that HAS a scope the old value could have ignored. I therefore judge 166.8 correct.

residual_uncertainty.why: The damage type and the direction (dealt vs received) of combat/events[13] are not observable from data/ or docs/math-foundations.md; the scenario definition lives in scripts/, which this runbook forbids reading. The verdict rests on Unmake being magic-only, enemy-side and once-applied, plus the fact that the delta is a pure 1.12 with the 7% Vulnerable factor unchanged.
residual_uncertainty.falsifier: If combat/events[13] is a MAGIC damage event dealt by any participant (including an ally) to an enemy champion that is inside the Unmake aura, and the x1.12 was applied only once in the old baseline, then the old value 186.8 is correct and the new value drops an amp the wiki explicitly grants 'from all sources'. Checking the event's damage_type and its attacker/defender pair in the golden event ledger settles it immediately.
residual_uncertainty.secondary_alternative: If Bloodletter's Curse is in this scenario's loadout, the delta could instead be a Vile Decay stack-attribution change (per-target stacks no longer shared across the roster) against an enemy whose rounded MR is 85, 90/91, or >=180. That reading also makes the NEW value correct (stacks are applied per target by dealing magic ability damage to that target), so it does not change the verdict.
